construct: marginal contribution of external J-space (v0.5 checkpoint-only, v1 incremental projection) to post-compaction state survival, versus Pi built-in compaction baseline

arms.plain: Pi built-in compaction only (runnable today, no J-space code required)
arms.v05_checkpoint: five-field checkpoint written at forced compaction boundary, injected after compaction
arms.v1_incremental: v0.5 plus per-turn deterministic projection refresh and file-level stale marking; per-turn model patch stays behind GO gate
arms.current: Current student-agent product baseline: Pi built-in compaction plus the existing Context Runtime / memory system prefix; used for migration value, not as the causal plain baseline

input.description: Run probe-instrumented long tasks with harness-forced compaction at fixed boundaries.
setup: Tasks: extend long-context-maintenance plus 2 new probe tasks (see review-notes)
Force compaction deterministically after phase 2 and phase 4 via harness control, never rely on natural overflow
Plant three probe types per task: turn-1-only constraint (git-diff verifiable), decoy path with signature error (countable in events.jsonl), cross-boundary next-step dependency
seeds >= 3 per arm per task; identical model, temperature, tier config across arms
Preflight Step -1: verify the pinned Pi version's real compaction path, hooks, session lifecycle, provider payload order, and protected-trace observability
Add a current product-baseline arm; plain must explicitly disable the existing Context Runtime/model-side memory injection
Generate and validate a per-task leakage_manifest.json so cross-boundary conclusions are absent from files, later phase instructions, automatic recall, and oracle errors
Run a 3-5-call API usage probe before the main baseline; preserve raw provider usage and compare it with Pi-exposed usage

expectedBehavior: v0.5 improves constraint survival and goal continuation over plain; v1 additionally reduces repeated decoy-path attempts. Expected split: constraint/goal metrics move at v0.5, rejected-path metrics only move if projection carries them.
passCondition: Descriptive only; per-metric GO gate, no composite score. GO for v0.5 requires constraint_violation and phase_completion improve vs plain across >=2 tasks and >=2 seeds without cost regression beyond budget. v1 GO judged only on repeated_failed_path and stale-related metrics, per ADR-style metric separation.

grader.path: scripts/eval-jspace-recovery-runner.ts (to be written; reads events.jsonl + git diff + protected trace, no LLM grader at runtime)

oracle.path: per-task solution/solve.sh; adversarial/known-bad = post-compaction constraint violation replay; adversarial/alternative-valid = different valid route completing all phases

failureImplication: If plain arm shows no constraint loss or repetition at forced compaction boundaries, the J-space premise is unsupported for this harness; close GO gate before writing implementation code.
relatedPaper: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation (unreliability +112%, recap recovers 15-20%); Meta-Harness (trace-based attribution over scores-only)
relatedAdr: ADR-002 (attribution table protocol; tombstone scope clarified in review-notes)
ADR-003 (P0-style zero-cost premise check via plain arm)
regressionRisk: Forced compaction hook may itself alter baseline behavior; validate hook neutrality with a no-op arm on one task first
Probe constraints must be natural task requirements, not tripwires undiscoverable from instruction (Gate 1 rule)
A run may be mislabeled plain while still carrying the existing memory system prefix; require a protected feature manifest
Cross-boundary conclusions may leak through files, later prompts, automatic recall, or oracle errors
Framework/provider adapters may append content after the dynamic checkpoint and invalidate cache comparisons

stepMinusOne: Inspect the pinned Pi dependency, not upstream main, for compaction hooks and per-call context APIs
Prove forced compaction uses the same path as production compaction
Capture final provider payload ordering and protected trace fields
Stop before Step 0 if the product path cannot be demonstrated

usageProbe.calls: 3-5 real LLM calls with at least one tool call
usageProbe.policy: BigModel may validate instrumentation only; final behavioral conclusions use the selected experiment provider/model

plain: Existing Context Runtime/model-side memory prefix disabled
No Task Ledger, Recall, checkpoint, or J-space content injected into the model
current: Used to measure migration value versus today's product behavior
armIsolation.manifest: Write the actual enabled feature set for every run to protected trace

forbiddenChannels: automatically recalled Task Ledger or Working Memory entries
oracle or test errors that reveal the conclusion

requirements: Checkpoint/J-space is the final serialized content block
No framework or retry injection follows it
It is not persisted in ordinary conversation history
The prior call's dynamic block is removed
Cache breakpoint precedes the dynamic block
Dynamic block itself is not cache-controlled

executionOrder: Step -1: pinned Pi/product-path and provider-payload audit
Step 0: forced-compaction harness plus no-op neutrality check
Step 1: plain x3 seeds plus a small current product-baseline sample
Step 2: implement and compare v0.5 against plain/current
Step 3: implement v1 deterministic projection only after v0.5 GO
Step 4: consider per-turn model patch only if repeated-path metrics remain unchanged
